claims.text: The initial material is a single-phase fcc FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy.
Introducing a secondary phase into single-phase fcc FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloys will increase coercive field.
Grain refinement of single-phase fcc FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloys will increase coercive field.
Carbides or oxides can provide the proposed secondary phase.
Mechanical alloying or spark plasma sintering can produce the proposed refined-grain composite microstructure.
The intervention will create either a secondary phase or a refined grain structure.
The introduced secondary phase will pin magnetic domain walls.
Grain refinement will reduce magnetic domain size.
Domain-wall pinning will increase coercive field.
Reduction of magnetic domain size will increase coercive field.
The modified alloy will exhibit a 20% coercive-field increase relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a matched derivative.
The coercive field will increase from 100 Oe to 120 Oe at room temperature.
Porosity and defects may affect coercivity in the modified alloys.

contradictions.description: The proposal does not isolate a single intervention: it alternates between secondary-phase introduction and grain refinement, which are distinct interventions with different mediators and mechanisms.

A 20% increase is equated with an absolute threshold of 120 Oe even though the baseline is allowed to be either FeCoNi or an unspecified matched derivative. The 120 Oe threshold is equivalent to 20% only when the measured baseline is exactly 100 Oe.
